question:
Three finite sets are used in a function-mapping activity: $X=\{1,2,3\}$, $Y=\{a,b,c\}$ and $Z=\{p,q,r\}$. A function $f:X\to Y$ is defined by $f(1)=a$, $f(2)=b$, $f(3)=c$, while $g:Y\to Z$ is defined by $g(a)=q$, $g(b)=r$, $g(c)=p$. Each element of the codomain of each function occurs exactly once as an image. Students study the composite transformation from $X$ to $Z$ and then determine how the original elements can be recovered. They also compare the inverse of the composite function with applying the two inverse functions in reverse order.

(a) Find $gof(1)$, $gof(2)$ and $gof(3)$.

(b) Write $f^{-1}$ and $g^{-1}$ by specifying the image of every element in their domains.

(c) Determine $(gof)^{-1}$.

(d) Verify for every element of $Z$ that $(gof)^{-1}=f^{-1}og^{-1}$.
explanation:
(a)
$gof(1)=g(f(1))=g(a)=q$. Similarly, $gof(2)=g(b)=r$ and $gof(3)=g(c)=p$. Therefore, $gof$ is given by $1\mapsto q$, $2\mapsto r$ and $3\mapsto p$.

(b)
Since $f(1)=a$, $f(2)=b$ and $f(3)=c$, its inverse is $f^{-1}(a)=1$, $f^{-1}(b)=2$ and $f^{-1}(c)=3$. Since $g(a)=q$, $g(b)=r$ and $g(c)=p$, its inverse is $g^{-1}(q)=a$, $g^{-1}(r)=b$ and $g^{-1}(p)=c$.

(c)
From part (a), $gof$ maps $1$ to $q$, $2$ to $r$ and $3$ to $p$. Reversing these pairs gives $(gof)^{-1}(q)=1$, $(gof)^{-1}(r)=2$ and $(gof)^{-1}(p)=3$.

(d)
For $q\in Z$, $f^{-1}(g^{-1}(q))=f^{-1}(a)=1=(gof)^{-1}(q)$. For $r\in Z$, $f^{-1}(g^{-1}(r))=f^{-1}(b)=2=(gof)^{-1}(r)$. For $p\in Z$, $f^{-1}(g^{-1}(p))=f^{-1}(c)=3=(gof)^{-1}(p)$. Hence, for every element of $Z$, $(gof)^{-1}=f^{-1}og^{-1}$.
